harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured daily logrotate for /var/log/inventory/app.log on node1 with 7 compressed rotations and copytruncate (keeps the file descriptor valid so the app can keep writing post-rotation). Validated with logrotate dry-run, forced live rotations (verified compression via delaycompress, 7-rotation cap with oldest pruning, and continued writes to app.log after rotation), then restored original log content. Completed mandatory restart evidence: captured boot_id baseline, rebooted node1, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified the logrotate config, timer, and log content all persisted post-reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected /var/log/inventory/app.log and confirmed logrotate 3.21.0 present with logrotate.timer active/enabled
Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app with daily, rotate 7, compress, delaycompress, missingok, notifempty, copytruncate
Validated config via `logrotate -d` dry-run
Forced 8 successive rotations to confirm: writes continue after rotation, delaycompress compresses on the following cycle, and rotation count caps at exactly 7 with oldest pruned
Restored original app.log content after testing
Captured pre-restart boot_id, logrotate config, app.log content, and timer status as baseline
Rebooted node1 via `systemctl reboot` backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec access returned
Verified boot_id changed (92ec88af... -> c033c533...) proving an actual restart
Verified post-restart recovery: logrotate config intact, app.log content intact, logrotate.timer active and enabled, dry-run still validates

evidence.requirement: Daily rotation with 7 compressed rotations configured for /var/log/inventory/app.log
evidence.summary: Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app (daily, rotate 7, compress, delaycompress, copytruncate) and validated with logrotate dry-run

evidence.requirement: Application can continue writing after rotation
evidence.summary: Forced rotation via copytruncate; confirmed app.log truncated in place and new writes succeeded immediately after rotation

evidence.requirement: Retention capped at 7 rotations with compression applied
evidence.summary: Ran 7 total forced rotations; observed app.log.1 through app.log.7.gz present, then an 8th rotation kept the count at exactly 7 (oldest pruned)
Captured boot_id, logrotate config, app.log content, and active logrotate.timer before restart

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnection
evidence.summary: Backgrounded `systemctl reboot` with a short delay so the exec call returned successfully before the node dropped

evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity after restart
evidence.summary: Connection timed out during reboot, then subsequent poll succeeded with boot_id changed from 92ec88af... to c033c533...

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of logrotate config, log data, and timer
evidence.summary: Confirmed /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app content intact, app.log content intact, logrotate.timer active/enabled, and dry-run still validates the rule post-reboot
